memory_update.text: FORM should be tracked as an HBM probe-card / advanced-package test candidate; strongest next verification is HBM-specific revenue or customer commentary.

ONTO is a higher-attention but still non-mega-cap process-control candidate with direct AI advanced-packaging evidence through PACE and HBM-related revenue commentary.
AEIS is best used as a reference anchor for RF/DC plasma power subsystems inside semiconductor tools; direct AI exposure needs more granular segment evidence.

Next Layer 1B/1C searches should test additional smaller names in burn-in/test, plating/cleaning, cleanroom components, substrates, and specialty consumables, including COHU, AEHR, ACMR, ICHR, UCTT, MKSI, ENTG, and AMKR where market-cap and evidence fit.

AEIS should remain in the underfollowed lane for advanced packaging and HBM-adjacent semiconductor equipment research because provided context directly links it to RF/DC power systems for etch and deposition tools.
MKSI is a candidate for process-control and instrumentation exposure, but its direct AI/HBM packaging linkage needs stronger evidence from company filings or customer/tool-OEM disclosures.

ENTG is a candidate for fab consumables and specialty materials exposure, with the key next test being whether AI-related leading-edge logic, HBM, or advanced packaging is visible in disclosed growth drivers.

This pass lacks primary-source verification from 10-Ks, 10-Qs, earnings transcripts, investor presentations, and tool-OEM customer disclosures; all underfollowed candidates should be upgraded or removed after primary-source checks.

FORM should remain a high-priority underfollowed candidate for the advanced-packaging/HBM-test node because probe cards and wafer test directly intersect known-good-die economics for AI accelerators and HBM stacks.

COHU should remain in the Layer 1 universe as an HBM inspection/metrology and semiconductor test-automation candidate, but survival to Layer 2 requires evidence that HBM-related Neon adoption is material to orders or revenue.

PDFS is a non-obvious software/data candidate for process-control and yield analytics across fab, test, assembly, and packaging data; key open issue is whether AI/HBM/advanced-packaging exposure is material rather than thematic.

VECO is a niche process-equipment candidate with explicit investor-presentation mapping to AI GPU, HBM DRAM, and advanced packaging; next pass should verify production-tool-of-record depth and customer concentration.

Advanced packaging and HBM test appear to create second-order bottlenecks in probe cards, inspection/metrology, process-control data, and specialized process equipment, not only in headline GPU or HBM chip supply.

Need a separate Layer 1B pass for RF/DC power subsystems and fab consumables, including AEIS, MKSI, ENTG, specialty chemicals, and cleanroom/filtration suppliers; this pass prioritized HBM test, probe, metrology, process-control software, and packaging process tools.

FORM should remain a high-priority underfollowed candidate for the advanced-packaging/HBM-test node because company materials directly tie its probe cards to HBM, known-good-die, interposer, and advanced-packaging test flows.

ONTO should remain in the discovery lane as a process-control and inspection/metrology candidate for AI-related advanced packaging, with later-layer work focused on revenue purity and HBM customer evidence.
COHU is a lower-attention HBM inspection/test automation candidate; survival to later layers depends on proving that the Neon HBM platform is commercially material.

ACMR is a speculative-shadow candidate for advanced-packaging wet processing, TSV, and plating exposure; the key gap is whether this maps to meaningful AI/HBM customer demand rather than generic semiconductor capex.
Next search pass should separately examine RF/DC power subsystems and fab consumables using AEIS, MKSI, ENTG, ICHR, UCTT, and specialty-chemicals suppliers as starting anchors.
